body.claim: Once you know how something turned out, it feels as if it was predictable all along.
body.why: This is hindsight bias: the tendency to see past events as more predictable than they were. In a study around Nixon's trip to Beijing and Moscow, people later overestimated the likelihood they had given to outcomes that actually happened. In a 1975 method, people read a story with four outcomes, were told one was true, and then rated that one as more likely.

probes.question: True or false: after being told which outcome of a story is true, people tend to rate that outcome as more likely.
